headline: Anchorage Code Can’t Answer / What The Cameras Collect

eval_history.note: far ridge sliced headline line 2 in half; posterized water read as camouflage blobs with rain-like threads over it; gantry legs caged the focal; 750 FEEDS label dark-on-dark
headline, gantry air and the closed bay all fixed; water still camouflage-blobbed (the field stretch cancelled itself out), ridges too close in value, HELD tag collided with the deck

water fixed (true anisotropic braid strip over a graded slack pool); but the draw-down current lines read as scratches, the tag's eyelet was drawn on top of its own last glyph, and the load read as a suitcase rather than slung freight

scratches, tag eyelet and the suitcase read all fixed (spreader bar + lifting slings); grayscale check showed the white flow curtains out-punching the amber focal, and the sling had no visible air between spreader and load
bays now read as dark apertures and the amber focal wins the grayscale check; but the spreader bar spanning the load read as a canopy/roof — the assembly looked like a shelter, not a lift
spreader replaced with a wide angled sling to two shackles and the load given an asymmetric equipment face (stencil plate left, louvred bay right) — reads as slung freight mid-lift. Ships.

eval_final.note: Headline is poster-scale and cleanly legible but sits on the sky rather than interlocking with the terrain; the planned ridge/baseline overlap was abandoned in iteration 2 because it was destroying line 2. Legibility was the right trade.
